name: drishti-app
//: @kolu/surface-app is NOT a bun dependency — like @kolu/surface, @kolu/surface-remote, @kolu/surface-map, @kolu/surface-daemon, and @kolu/surface-daemon-supervisor it is hydrated into node_modules/@kolu/* (raw .ts sources; no build step). Sourced hermetically from the npins-pinned kolu tree (npins/sources.json → kolu): nix/overlay.nix extracts each as a nix-store path, nix/env.nix exports $DRISHTI_KOLU_*, and the dev shell / install recipe / build derivation copy them into node_modules. Runtime dependencies of those hydrated sources are declared here; `effect` + `@effect/platform-node` carry the whole RPC/schema/transport stack AND the parent's HTTP server (surface-app serves the fresh shell as `effect/http` LAYERS now — hono and @hono/node-server are gone from kolu and from here), pinned to the EXACT version the hydrated sources declare; neverthrow carries Surface Remote's explicit agent-source result, quick-lru bounds its successful derivation cache, split2 frames child output, ts-pattern keeps its closed state folds exhaustive (and supervisor convergence), and dequal backs Surface Map's STRUCTURAL republish gate (kolu#2022). @kolu/solid-pwa-install is hydrated the same way. UW3: surface-daemon-supervisor powers convergeAdmit / probeDaemonIdentityFrom on the parent; the agent half lives in the agent package via surface-daemon. SOLID 2: the hydrated client sources (@kolu/surface's solid helpers, @kolu/surface-map, @kolu/surface-app/solid, @kolu/solid-pwa-install) import `solid-js` 2 AND `@solidjs/web` — the DOM renderer is its own package now, so `render` and the JSX runtime live there — plus `@solid-primitives/rootless` (surface's keyed subscription cache) and `@solid-primitives/scheduled`. All four are declared here at the majors those sources name, so the hydrated tree and this app resolve ONE copy of each; a second copy of solid-js would give the hydrated subscriptions their own reactive graph, which this app's memos would never see. `@solidjs/babel-plugin` replaces `babel-preset-solid` (Solid 2 ships its JSX compiler as a plugin, defaulting to `moduleName: "@solidjs/web"`); it stays a runtime dep because the SERVER's build.ts compiles the client bundle at boot.
